# Switchres timing calculator

These six source files come from the `deps/switchres` directory of Antonio Giner's RetroArch `mister` branch at commit `da4ff7e03184079f5c3715d48e441503a5d6675f`. The import normalizes line endings and trailing whitespace. The upstream notices name Chris Kennedy, Antonio Giner, Alexandre Wodarczyk, and Gil Delescluse and specify GPL-2.0-or-later. See [the upstream source](https://github.com/antonioginer/RetroArch/tree/da4ff7e03184079f5c3715d48e441503a5d6675f/deps/switchres) and the [GPL v2 text](COPYING).

MiSTerCast builds `modeline.cpp`, `monitor.cpp`, and `log.cpp` in a static calculation library. The adapter uses `modeline_create()` and `monitor_set_preset()`. It never initializes the Switchres display manager, wrapper, or platform backends. It constrains the candidate active area, preserves the half-line convention, and checks the final clock and timings before sending the existing Groovy_MiSTer packet.

The adapter checks the 8-bit porch and sync register widths and accounts for integer rounding when the receiver's PLL can't find an admissible fractional multiplier. These constraints follow the Groovy_MiSTer HPS and FPGA code at commit `b0c8bc8a2fb45eed75580fdfb3692d6815d08821`. The existing mode packet has no acknowledgement for the applied raster. A loopback test can check command order and frame geometry, while physical CRT sync and PLL lock require a MiSTer. [Groovy_MiSTer source](https://github.com/asdgdg355235/Groovy_MiSTer/tree/b0c8bc8a2fb45eed75580fdfb3692d6815d08821)

The combined MiSTerCast build that links Switchres is distributed under [GPL-3.0-or-later](../../COPYING). The [Unlicense](../../LICENSE) continues to apply to the original MiSTerCast files. AVIR retains its MIT terms. Binary redistribution must meet the applicable GPL source and notice requirements, including access to the corresponding MiSTerCast and Switchres sources and the build instructions.

## CRU timing reference

The CRT, Exact CRT, CVT, GTF, and actual rate calculations were reviewed in ToastyX's Custom Resolution Utility mirror at commit `00693a119a4f7dd5787f4f69e26aed5e603e2957`, which carries GPL-3.0-or-later. CRU's Automatic CRT mode uses a table first, then CVT-standard blanking. Exact CRT adjusts the totals and derives the clock from the requested cadence. MiSTerCast uses the same clock and total relationships for verification, with Switchres's monitor ranges and porch durations controlling generation. For example, CRU's 640×480p60 table entry has 800 horizontal and 525 vertical total pixels and lines, which gives a 31.5 kHz line rate and fails a 15 kHz range. MiSTerCast imports zero CRU source files. [CRU source](https://github.com/kreier/cru/blob/00693a119a4f7dd5787f4f69e26aed5e603e2957/CRU/CRU/DetailedResolutionClass.cpp)
